_comment: SYNTHETIC DATA — fabricated for portfolio demonstration only. Not a real alert.
alert_name: Phishing Email Campaign — Auth Failure + Suspicious Attachment or Link
escalation_condition: Critical if proxy POST event follows email delivery (credential submission suspected)
description: Detects phishing email campaigns targeting internal users based on email authentication failures (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) combined with high-risk attachment types or suspicious URLs. A secondary proxy-layer signal fires when a user clicks a URL from a suspicious email and submits a form (GET + POST pattern), indicating possible credential harvesting.

variants.name: Spearphishing Attachment
variants.description: Email fails SPF and DKIM, contains a macro-enabled or high-risk attachment, and was sent to 2+ recipients from the same source.
variants.threshold: SPFResult IN (FAIL, SOFTFAIL) AND DKIMResult IN (FAIL, NONE) AND AttachmentExtension IN high_risk_list AND RecipientCount >= 2

variants.name: Spearphishing Link — Gateway
variants.description: Email delivered despite SPF/DKIM failure; contains URLs with uncategorised, newly-registered, or suspicious domains.
variants.threshold: SPFResult IN (FAIL, SOFTFAIL) AND URLCount > 0 AND URLCategory IN (UNCATEGORIZED, NEWLY_REGISTERED, SUSPICIOUS, PHISHING) AND RecipientCount >= 2

variants.name: Spearphishing Link — Proxy Click
variants.description: User clicked a URL from a suspicious email; proxy logs show HTTP GET followed by POST within 60 seconds — consistent with form submission to a credential harvester.
variants.threshold: ProxyGET to uncategorised/suspicious URL + ProxyPOST to same host within 60 seconds, correlated to prior suspicious email delivery
variants.default_action: Escalate to Critical; initiate credential compromise response

required_fields.description: Time the email was processed by the gateway or click was logged by proxy.
Envelope sender address. Check domain against known-legitimate list and lookalike patterns.
Recipient address. Used for campaign breadth calculation and targeted account triage.
SPF authentication result: PASS, FAIL, SOFTFAIL, NONE. FAIL or SOFTFAIL required to fire.
DKIM signature validation: PASS, FAIL, NONE. FAIL or NONE required (with SPF FAIL) to fire.
DMARC policy result and enforcement action. Determines whether gateway blocked or delivered.
Attachment filename; extension is matched against high-risk list. Required for Variant A.
SHA-256 of attachment. Used for campaign correlation (same hash across recipients) and IOC submission.
URLs extracted from email body. Domain used for category lookup and proxy correlation. Required for Variant B.

enrichment_steps: WHOIS / passive DNS lookup on sender domain: check registration date, registrar, and nameservers.
Threat intel lookup on SourceIP: check for prior phishing infrastructure, bulletproof hosting, or known malicious ASN.
Threat intel lookup on AttachmentHash: check against public sandbox reports (e.g., VirusTotal) for known malware family.
Threat intel lookup on URL domain: check for prior phishing reports, certificate transparency (new cert = new domain), and hosting details.
Correlate URL with proxy logs: identify all users who received the email and determine which clicked.
For Variant B2: check Active Directory for recent successful logons for affected users — credential submission may precede unauthorized access.

recommended_actions.action: Quarantine or recall all emails in campaign
recommended_actions.detail: For Variant A: confirm gateway quarantine is in place. For Variant B: initiate email recall from all recipient mailboxes if the gateway supports it. Prevent users from accessing the email.

recommended_actions.action: Block sender domain and source IP at the email gateway
recommended_actions.detail: Add sender domain (e.g., hr-documents.example) and SourceIP (203.0.113.20) to the gateway blocklist. These should be scoped to block, not tag-and-deliver.

recommended_actions.action: Block URL and URL domain at the web proxy
recommended_actions.detail: Add the phishing URL and its domain to the proxy blocklist. For per-recipient token URLs, block at the domain level.

recommended_actions.action: Block attachment hash at email gateway and EDR
recommended_actions.detail: For Variant A: submit AttachmentHash to EDR custom IOC list and email gateway attachment blocklist. Prevents re-delivery or execution on endpoints.

recommended_actions.action: Force password reset for users who clicked and submitted (Variant B2)
recommended_actions.detail: Users with a POST event in proxy logs should be treated as potentially compromised. Force immediate password reset and verify MFA is enrolled before re-enabling access. Check for active sessions originating from unexpected IPs.

Send a targeted security notification to all users who received the phishing email, explaining what to do if they clicked or opened the attachment. Do not use a public-facing announcement — targeted awareness reduces secondary incidents.

false_positive_notes: Common benign triggers: marketing platforms with poor email auth hygiene, phishing simulation campaigns (allowlist simulation vendor IPs), vendor invoice emails from shared SMTP infrastructure. See detection.md for full guidance.
